entities.summary:
Rumbaudas Valimantaitis was a Lithuanian noble of Zadora coat of arms, son of Valimantas and brother of Mykolas Kęsgaila. He became a prominent figure in Samogitian politics, serving as Elder of Samogitia from 1409 to 1411 and Grand Marshal from 1412 to 1432.


 As Elder, Valimantaitis played a crucial role in maintaining the autonomy of Samogitia, a region in modern-day Lithuania, during a tumultuous period of Lithuanian history. His leadership helped to preserve the region's unique cultural identity and its traditional way of life.


 Valimantaitis's legacy extends beyond his administrative roles, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of education. His contributions to the cultural and intellectual life of Samogitia have had a lasting impact on the region's heritage.


 Despite his significant influence on Samogitian politics, Valimantaitis's life and achievements remain somewhat overshadowed by the more prominent figures of his time. Nevertheless, his legacy as a champion of local autonomy and cultural preservation continues to inspire historians and scholars today.
